body:
It's an issue with zlib: https://github.com/bazelbuild/bazel/blob/17770e5d78e640e419194504293df563d77ccf8c/third_party/zlib/trees.c#L530

It sounds like it's probably harmless:
* https://bugs.openjdk.java.net/browse/JDK-6358524
* https://bugzilla.mozilla.org/show_bug.cgi?id=431950
Also, the log message only appears in debug builds. Shouldn't Bazel be shipping an opt build of singlejar?
Thanks Liam for tracking this down. Since this is not a bazel issue, can we close this @damienmg ? It's definitely neither a release blocker nor a P1 bug.

I'd vote for not closing it, but bringing it down to P2 and removing the release blocker.

It is quite annoying, because this happens during all Java builds with the released Bazel binary.
We should make sure to compile zlib using a #define that disables these trace messages.
It's not clear to me why we only get this output with this release and not before, since we only had one zlib version until now. Is JavaBuilder built differently now?

Ha! Found the reason: https://github.com/bazelbuild/bazel/commit/d894345ed88f8adce600b66a310b5210d0bcb59c

That's actually a great change that I wanted to make myself, but couldn't get around to. The C++ version of SingleJar should be much faster than the Java one. Now we just have to get rid of the message. :)

A regression that output a lot of garbage output is definitely a P1 and
should be fixed by the next release. Since the message is harmless can we
simply swallow it in C++ singlejar?
